title: Switzerland – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – EPFL - Entreprise Totale - Assainissement et bouclage d'un réseau d'eaux industrielles, y.c. création d'une station de découplage hydraulique au bord du lac contre la lutte de la propagation des Moules Quagga
description: Le marché porte sur l’étude et la construction en Entreprise Totale des parties d’ouvrages suivantes : 1. Nouvelle station de découplage (SDD) y compris les adaptations hydrauliques dans les stations de pompage (SPP), les conduites de liaison SPP et SDD et les conduites de rejet au lac entre le bâtiment SDD et la chambre de visite d’interface des conduites CCU/SDD. 2. Nouvelles conduites de liaison (terrestres) SDD-PDR jusqu’au poste de redistribution PDR, y compris la création d’un nouveau local de pompes dans l’actuel parking au sous-sol du bâtiment BS de l’EPFL. 3. Rénovation du réseau de distribution dans les galeries EPFL depuis le poste PDR jusqu’aux différentes sous-stations propres à chaque bâtiment du campus y compris la nouvelle conduite de retour et les adaptations hydrauliques à la CCT. L’Entreprise Totale interviendra de la phase « 32. Projet d’ouvrage » jusqu’à la phase « 53. Mise en service, achèvement ». L’élément déclencheur et l’objectif primordial du projet est la protection contre la prolifération des moules Quagga dans nos conduites et la sécurisation du réseau de refroidissement. Cependant, la vétusté des conduites ainsi que nos capacités en refroidissement actuelles, induisent une réflexion globale sur l’avenir de l’ensemble du site de l’EPFL et l’UNIL à Ecublens. De ce fait, le projet comprend les trois objectifs ci-dessous : 1. Protection totale des conduites du réseau de refroidissement contre la prolifération des moules Quagga, grâce au découplage hydraulique et à un nouveau réseau en boucle fermée. 2. Augmentation des capacités en refroidissement afin de subvenir aux besoins futurs dus aux nouveaux bâtiments et à l’augmentation de la demande des bâtiments existants. 3. Réduction des coûts d’exploitation et optimisation énergétique grâce au bouclage du réseau. Veuillez consulter le cahier des charges et ses annexes pour plus de renseignement.

Les prestations, objets du présent accord-cadre, répondent aux besoins actuels de la Communauté urbaine du Grand Reims et de la Ville de Reims et aux besoins éventuels des autres adhérents à la Centrale d’achat .Le présent accord-cadre est conclu pour une durée de 48 mois à compter de sa date de notification et au plus tôt le 1er avril 2027. Le lot n°2 est multi-attributaires : sous réserve de la réception d’un nombre suffisant d’offres régulières, adaptées et acceptables, il sera conclu au maximum avec TROIS (3) opérateurs économiques. Ce lot sera intégralement exécuté par la conclusion de marchés subséquents, dans les conditions fixées aux articles R. 2162-7 à R. 2162-12 du code de la commande publique. Les lots 1 et 3 sont mono-attributaires : chaque lot sera conclu avec un seul opérateur économique. description:

title: 2026- Åpen tilbudskonkurranse - Leie og drift av sykehjemsplasser - Reservert for ideelle organisasjoner
description: Oppdragsgiver skal i tråd med politisk vedtak anskaffe 60-100 sykehjemsplasser for personer med demens og somatiske langtidsbehov.Det skal inngås leieavtale og tjenesteytingsavtale med en og samme leverandør. Det er en forutsetning for kontrakten at valgt leverandør fremskaffer, eier og stiller til disposisjon nødvendige lokaler på Askøy for tjenesteutførelsen. Leverandøren skal påta seg et totalansvar for å levere (utforme, prosjektere, bygge og leie ut), samt forvalte, drifte og vedlikeholde sykehjemmet.Konkurransen er reservert for ideelle organisasjoner, jf. anskaffelsesforskriften § 30-2a.Vi gjør oppmerksom på at det i kunngjøringsskjemaet er opplyst at det er en åpen anbudskonkurranse. Dette er fordi det per i dag ikke er teknisk mulig å velge prosedyren "åpen tilbudskonkurranse" i kunngjøringsskjemaet når skjema eForm 20 Helse- og sosialtjenester benyttes. Vi understreker imidlertid at prosedyren som skal benyttes er "åpen tilbudskonkurranse".

title: Åpenhet og inkludering - politiets samhandling med hele befolkningen
description: Formålet med forskningsoppdraget er å fremskaffe kunnskap om hvordan ulike grupper av befolkningen opplever politiet, hvilke forhold som påvirker samspillet mellom politi og innbyggere, og hvordan politiet kan sikre at ulike perspektiver og erfaringer blir hørt og ivaretatt. Det er behov for kunnskap om hvorvidt det er grupper som opplever at de ikke blir hørt, hvordan politiet når ut til grupper som i liten grad selv tar kontakt med politiet på eget initiativ og hvordan ulike former for kommunikasjon og dialog oppleves av ulike grupper. Forskningen skal gi et bedre kunnskapsgrunnlag for hvordan politiet kan styrke dialogen med befolkningen, tilpasse kommunikasjon og arbeidsformer til ulike målgrupper og utvikle tjenester som ivaretar rettssikkerhet, likebehandling og høy kvalitet. Forskningen skal også bidra med kunnskap om sammenheng mellom åpenhet, inkludering, tillit og politiets legitimitet, samt hvilken betydning dette kan ha for samfunnets motstandskraft. Se mer informasjon i konkurransegrunnlaget.

buyer: De Werkvennootschap NV van publiek recht
title: Belgium – Construction work – DBFM Contract relating to the comprehensive renovation of the Rupel Tunnel
description: The DBFM Contract relating to the comprehensive renovation of the Rupel Tunnel is part of the Flanders Tunnel Plan. As part of the Flanders Tunnel Plan, the Agency for Roads and Traffic has developed a master plan aimed at ensuring the safety and reliability of all tunnels in Flanders over a ten-year period, modernising their operation and introducing professional asset management in accordance with ISO 55001. Comprehensive renovations constitute one of the four pillars of the Flanders Tunnel Plan. A comprehensive renovation, including the comprehensive renovation of the Rupel Tunnel, combines all structural and civil engineering works with the renewal of technical installations designed to enhance safety. For the purposes of the present procurement procedure, the Agency for Roads and Traffic and De Werkvennootschap have entered into a cooperation arrangement under which De Werkvennootschap makes its knowledge and expertise available to the Agency for Roads and Traffic. In this context, De Werkvennootschap has been authorised to conduct the present Procurement Procedure in the name and on behalf of the Agency for Roads and Traffic. For the purposes of awarding the Contract, the Agency for Roads and Traffic will be represented by De Werkvennootschap, which will act vis-à-vis third parties as the Agency’s authorised representative and as the central and sole point of contact, unless expressly stated otherwise.

title: Netherlands – Sanitary dispensing machines – Sanitaire voorzieningen
description: De gemeente Utrecht wil een Raamovereenkomst afsluiten met één Opdrachtnemer voor het leveren, plaatsen, onderhouden en verwijderen van kwalitatief hoogwaardige sanitaire voorzieningen tegen een optimale prijs-kwaliteitverhouding, die voldoen aan de gestelde eisen in het Programma van Eisen. De gemeente heeft getracht de kwaliteit en uitstraling van de huidige sanitaire voorzieningen daarin vast te leggen en ambieert dat de nieuw te leveren sanitaire voorzieningen minimaal gelijkwaardig zijn aan de huidige kwaliteit en uitstraling. Denk hierbij aan levensduur, degelijkheid, kleur en afmetingen. De opsomming is niet limitatief. Daarnaast bevat de nieuwe Raamovereenkomst een juiste borging van de dienstverlening, duidelijke communicatie, ontzorging en verduurzaming. De gemeente verwacht over de gehele looptijd (maximaal 8 jaar) van de Raamovereenkomst sanitaire voorzieningen af te nemen met een verwachte totale waarde van € 3.600.000,- (excl. BTW). Dit komt neer op een jaarlijkse verwachte waarde van € 450.000 per jaar (dit bedrag is inclusief de jaarlijkse indexatie en hierbeneden genoemde optie). Optie: afname extra hygiëneboxen (is bij start Raamovereenkomst geen onderdeel van de implementatieperiode) In de bovenstaande raming is rekening gehouden met de mogelijke uitrol tijdens de looptijd van Raamovereenkomst van extra circa 500 hygiëneboxen, wat een verwachte waarde heeft van circa € 54.000,- per jaar, nader gespecificeerd in het Programma van Eisen (bijlage 7) en Invulformulier tarieven (bijlage 9).

title: APN - NORAD Northern Basing Infrastructure (NNBI), Nunavut
description: Advance Procurement Notice NORAD Northern Basing Infrastructure (NNBI)  Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform Design-Builders of an upcoming contract opportunity at Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut. The purpose of this APN is to allow Design-Builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Design-Builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services The Department of National Defence (DND) is investing in infrastructure developments for the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD) Modernization and Continental Defence at the Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut.  This infrastructure investment aims to ensure that the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) have the tools they need to achieve their security and sovereignty objectives. These improvements will enable advanced aircraft operations and quick mobilization in the North for NORAD missions.   The infrastructure requirements for the FOL Iqaluit will include the following but are not limited to:  Airfield improvements;   Hangars with aprons and taxiways;   Ammunition compounds;  Fuel facilities;   Accommodations, warehousing, planning, multi-purpose facilities, and support equipment;   Robust IT, Cyber, and Logistics infrastructure.     Preliminary rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimates for the various facility components for each locations are as follows, subject to revision: Total hangar space, ~ 7,500 m2 Fuel storage, between 500,000 and 750,000 litres Office space  500 m2 Ammunition Storage 600 m2 Accommodations 4,000 m2 Fire Hall 2,000 m2 Multi-purpose facilities 9,000 m2 Indoor storage (Total), 7,000 m2 Apron 60,000 m2 Total asphalt surface 72,000 m2 The delivery method for this infrastructure will be a Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract, with one MDB contract for the site and an estimated total contract value that may exceed $5B. This multi-year contract consists of the following sequential and/or concurrent phases and are not limited to:  Requirements validation, concept development, market analysis and planning activities.   Design Phase activities.  Construction Phase activities.   It is anticipated that the Request for Proposal (RFP) will include detailed evaluation criteria; however, these remain subject to change and will be finalized and fully described in the RFP documentation upon release. At a high level, it is expected that the RFP will assess proponents on demonstrated experience across a range of factors, including northern design and construction experience, experience delivering similar asset types (both within and outside of northern environments), and the integration of design and construction capabilities within a single team. Key personnel requirements will include demonstrated northern experience for certain roles. The evaluation of approach and methodology is expected to consider how proponents plan to successfully deliver projects in northern environments, including logistics, climate, and constructability considerations, as well as their approach to Indigenous participation based on principles of meaningful participation and mitigation of potential adverse effects. In addition to the technical evaluation, a formal interview process will be conducted to further assess team capability to successfully deliver the project in a northern environment. The terms and conditions of the contract will allow for self-performed work by the design-build team.    The MDB solicitation for Iqaluit is projected to be released in Fall 2027. This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by DND.   The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project.  To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the MDB contract. The IBP will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities.  Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a Design-Builder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance at the level of SECRET. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing Design-Builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, Design-Builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 87007; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the Design-Builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a Design-Builder: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the

title: ITS4US Deployment Accelerator
description: The Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) Joint Program Office (JPO) looks to accelerate the replication of innovative technology solutions developed by large-scale deployment projects that it sponsors. ITS JPO believes that successful demonstration of these solutions by multiple agencies validates the technology's maturity and readiness for broader implementation across the industry. The purpose of this Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is to award up to five (5) operational pilots that will test integrated technology solutions developed and deployed by the ITS4US Deployment Program. Each awardee will develop, test, and deploy solutions modeled on ITS4US deployment project documentation and its associated open-source software. In addition, the awardees will form a deployer cohort where they receive USDOT-funded technical support designed to accelerate implementation. Awardees can build faster, better, and cheaper by launching related efforts together, and use the insight of peers who have recently succeeded in addressing similar challenges. See Attachments for further information.

description: July 7, 2026: This is Amendment 0009 to solicitation 47QRCA23R0001 The General Services Administration (GSA), Federal Acquisition Service (FAS), Office of Acquisition Solutions Development (ASD), is issuing Amendment 0009 in accordance with RFO-2025-05 Supplement 1 FAR 5.101 for the One Acquisition Solution for Integrated Services Plus (OASIS+), Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multi-Agency Contracts (MAC). The System for Award Management (SAM.gov) is the official source for information about this procurement. The following documents and attachments are updated as a result of Amendment 0009: OASIS+ Small Business RFP (current as of Amendment 0009) SF30 (Amendment 0009) and Continuation Sheet Provisional Attachments J.P-1 OASIS+ Domain Qualifications Matrix and Scorecards J.P-2 FPDS Sample J.P-3 Project Verification Form J.P-4 Domains Auto-Relevant NAICS Codes and PSCs J.P-9 Cost/Price Template J.P-14 Lateral Springboarding Summary Sheet Contract Attachments J-2 Task Order, Transactional Data, and Contract Access Fee Reporting J-4 Department of Defense Required Provisions and Clauses for Task Orders J-5 Task Order Clause and Provision Matrix Consistent with Section H.11 of the OASIS+ RFP, GSA intends to maintain continuously open solicitations to support rolling admissions/on-ramping and to allow existing awardees, when eligible, to compete for additional Domains as Government needs evolve. Should GSA determine a need to close any domain or solicitation, the agency will provide public notification. Offerors are permitted to submit a single proposal for multiple domains under a single solicitation. There is no fixed timeline for award; timelines will vary based on the volume of proposals received and are subject to resource availability. Offerors must be registered and active in SAM.gov. All proposals must be submitted through the OASIS+ SubmissionPortal (OSP). The OSP is open for registration and submission of offers as of January 12, 2026. Registration information and submission instructions are provided at https://oasis.app.cloud.gov/. For questions related to registration or technical issues, offerors can contact client.support@apexlogic.com. Industry is instructed to review the solicitation requirements and all amendments before submitting an offer. Offerors submitting a new offer after issuance of Amendment 0009 must acknowledge all current amendments in the OSP by completing the required amendment acknowledgement action during offer submission. A signed SF 33 remains required as part of all offer submissions; however, a separate signed SF30 upload is not required for new offers submitted after issuance of Amendment 0009 unless otherwise directed by the Government. Offerors that submitted an offer prior to issuance of Amendment 0009 and who have not received a contract award or unsuccessful notice are required to acknowledge Amendment 0009 by signing this SF 30 and uploading the signed SF 30 in Symphony to the Business Factors section for the applicable RFP no later than July 15, 2026. Offerors with pending offers under more than one OASIS+ RFP must upload the signed SF30 to the Business Factors section of each applicable RFP for which acknowledgement is required. Offerors are responsible for ensuring that the signed SF30 uploaded for each pending offer corresponds to the correct OASIS+ RFP. Please follow the steps below to upload the signed SF 30 in Symphony: Login to Symphony at https://oasis.app.cloud.gov/. Navigate to My Company. Navigate to the Business Factors page. Ensure the "My Solicitation Preferences" field is set to any OASIS+ solicitation to display the appropriate factors. Scroll down to the Other Documents section to see the Amendment 9 SF30 factor for each solicitation. Click the Amendment 9 factor for solicitations submitted prior to Amendment 9 release (Example: "Amendment 9 SF30 - OASIS+ 8(a) Continuously Open"). Upload the signed SF30 document and select the checkbox to certify the claim for the factor. Click "Save and Claim" for the factor. The signed SF30 is required for amendment acknowledgement purposes only. Offerors shall not submit revised proposal documents, additional supporting documentation, or other proposal changes. Failure to submit the signed SF30 by the stated deadline may result in the offer being ineligible for further consideration. Offerors are solely responsible for reviewing and staying current with the solicitation and all amendments posted on SAM.gov. In the event of a conflict, the solicitation and amendments posted to this notice on SAM.gov take precedence over any information contained on other websites or prior communications. Any clarification that changes solicitation requirements will be issued, as appropriate, through a solicitation amendment. ***************************************************************************************** May 12, 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration�s Office of Acquisition Solutions Development (ASD) is pleased to announce the first Phase II apparent awardee notifications for OASIS+ Total Small Business Set-Aside. A consolidated list of Phase II apparent awardees for all OASIS+ contract families may be accessed on the Solicitations (continuously open) page (see �Links� section within this SAM.gov posting). This list will be updated with additional apparent awardees as award announcements continue to be made. Award notifications have been sent via email to offerors who have been determined successful in one or more proposed domains. Apparent awardees are reminded to ensure that their SAM.gov entity information is active, accurate, and complete at all times. The program plans to issue formal awards and notices to proceed (NTPs) to qualified contractors on or about May 22, 2026 after final legal reviews occur. The newly awarded contracts will be available for ordering in GSA eBuy one business day following the issuance of formal awards and NTPs and upon contractor registration within the Vendor Support Center (VSC), whichever is later. Contract awardees must register their contracts in VSC before they will be visible in eBuy and available for procurement. Please note that GSA continues to release answers to RFP questions deemed broadly beneficial and relevant on a regular basis on the program website Solicitations (continuously open) page. Questions related to the award announcements should be submitted via email to the OASIS+ Contracting Officers at oasisplusmods@gsa.gov. Please continue to monitor this OASIS+ Interact Community forum where you can join and subscribe to get notifications about announcements and program updates. For more information about the OASIS+ Program, visit: The OASIS+ website. The General Services Administration (GSA), Federal Acquisition Service (FAS), Office of Professional Services and Human Capital (PSHC) Categories, is pleased to issue an amendment in accordance with RFO-2025-05 FAR 5.101 for the reopening of the One Acquisition Solution for Integrated Services Plus (OASIS+), Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multi-Agency Contracts (MAC). The System for Award Management (SAM.gov) is the official source for information about this procurement. The OASIS+ HUBZone Small Business Set-Aside RFP consists of the following: OASIS+ HUBZone Small Business Set-Aside RFP SF30 (Amendment 0008) and Continuation Sheet Provisional Attachments J.P-1 OASIS+ Domain Qualifications Matrix and Scorecards J.P-2 FPDS Sample J.P-3 Project Verification Form J.P-4 Domains Auto-Relevant NAICS Codes and PSCs J.P-5 Functional Areas and Sub-Areas J.P-6 Past Performance Rating Form J.P-7 CTA Qualifications & MRCL List Template J.P-8 Direct Labor Rate Ranges J.P-9 Cost/Price Template J.P-10 Reserved J.P-11 Reserved J.P-12 Subcontractor Letter of Commitment Template J.P-13 Financial Data Input Template J.P-14 Lateral Springboarding Summary Sheet Contract Attachments J-1 Labor Categories and Bureau of Labor Statistics Standard Occupational Classifications J-2 Task Order, Transactional Data, and Contract Access Fee Reporting J-3 Cybersecurity & Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) Deliverables J-4 Department of Defense Required Provisions and Clauses for Task Orders J-5 Task Order Clause and Provision Matrix Consistent with Section H.11 of the OASIS+ RFP, GSA intends to maintain continuously open solicitations to support rolling admissions (on-ramping) and to allow existing awardees, when eligible, to compete for additional Domains as Government needs evolve. Should GSA determine a need to close any domain or solicitation vehicle, the agency will provide public notification. Offerors are permitted to submit a single proposal for multiple domains under a single solicitation. There is no fixed timeline for award; timelines will vary based on the volume of proposals received and are subject to resource availability. Offerors must be registered and active in SAM.gov. All proposals must be submitted through the OASIS+ Symphony Portal (OSP). The OSP is open for registration and submission of offers as of January 12, 2026. Registration information and submission instructions are provided at https://oasis-plus-eval.app.cloud.gov/. For questions related to registration or technical issues, offerors can contact client.support@apexlogic.com. Industry is instructed to review the solicitation requirements posted to SAM.gov before submitting an offer. Offerors will be required to acknowledge Amendment 0008 as part of their offer submission. The OASIS+ CO is the sole point of contact for all questions under this solicitation. Industry is welcome to submit any questions after carefully reviewing the RFP and registering in the OSP. Offerors must submit all questions regarding the solicitation via the OSP. GSA reserves the right to publicly discuss and publish, or simply consider, questions and comments regarding the RFP. Offerors are solely responsible for reviewing and staying current with the solicitation and all amendments posted on SAM.gov. In the event of a conflict, the solicitation and amendments posted to this notice on SAM.gov take precedence over any information contained on other websites or prior communications. Any clarification that changes solicitation requirements will be issued, as appropriate, through a solicitation amendment. To stay connected, join the OASIS+ Interact Community and follow us on X and LinkedIn (linked at the bottom of this post).

Registration information and submission instructions are provided at https://oasis.app.cloud.gov/. For questions related to registration or technical issues, offerors can contact client.support@apexlogic.com. Industry is instructed to review the solicitation requirements and all amendments before submitting an offer. Offerors submitting a new offer after issuance of Amendment 0009 must acknowledge all current amendments in the OSP by completing the required amendment acknowledgement action during offer submission. A signed SF 33 remains required as part of all offer submissions; however, a separate signed SF30 upload is not required for new offers submitted after issuance of Amendment 0009 unless otherwise directed by the Government. Offerors that submitted an offer prior to issuance of Amendment 0009 and who have not received a contract award or unsuccessful notice are required to acknowledge Amendment 0009 by signing this SF 30 and uploading the signed SF 30 in Symphony to the Business Factors section for the applicable RFP no later than July 15, 2026. Offerors with pending offers under more than one OASIS+ RFP must upload the signed SF30 to the Business Factors section of each applicable RFP for which acknowledgement is required. Scroll down to the Other Documents section to see the Amendment 9 SF30 factor for each solicitation. Click the Amendment 9 factor for solicitations submitted prior to Amendment 9 release (Example: "Amendment 9 SF30 - OASIS+ 8(a) Continuously Open"). Upload the signed SF30 document and select the checkbox to certify the claim for the factor. Click "Save and Claim" for the factor. The signed SF30 is required for amendment acknowledgement purposes only. Offerors shall not submit revised proposal documents, additional supporting documentation, or other proposal changes. Failure to submit the signed SF30 by the stated deadline may result in the offer being ineligible for further consideration. title: Multi Mission Surface Combatant (MMSC) Post Delivery Execution Yard (PDEY)
description: PAE Maritime Solicitation N61177-27-R-0003 for the execution of post-delivery availabilities on four (4) Multi Mission Surface Combatants (MMSC) during a 14-month Post Delivery (PD) period for each ship. To effectively and efficiently accomplish necessary industrial work, three availabilities are planned for each ship in the MMSC post-delivery schedule. At a minimum, this includes a Post Shakedown Availability (PSA) following MMSC transit from Marinette, Wisconsin and prior to Post Delivery Test & Trials (PDT&T), an Industrial Post Delivery Availability (IPDA) following PDT&T, and a Continuous Maintenance Availability (CMAV) at the conclusion of the post-delivery period. Also, concurrent Planned Maintenance Availabilities (PMAVs) may be tasked to the shipyard during these scheduled industrial availabilities. These availabilities will be accomplished under the Post Delivery Execution Yard (PDEY) Contract. Cost Plus Award Fee (CPAF) task orders will be issued to support Post Delivery work for MMSC 1-4. The PD Execution Yard Contractor responsibilities include: 1. Preparation and Management of PSA, IPDA, and CMAV 2. Drydocking of MMSC during PSA 3. Execution of PSA, IPDA, and CMAV as well as concurrent PMAVs 4. Post Repair Trials (PRT) at the conclusion of PSA 5. Emergent Work identified prior to or during the PSA 6. Providing test, trials, readiness, and inspection support for the PSA The Period of Performance of the contract is intended to cover the Post Delivery periods for all 4 MMSCs. See PIEE link for Solicitation and related attachments: https://piee.eb.mil/sol/xhtml/unauth/search/oppMgmtLink.xhtml?noticeId=N6117727R0003&noticeType=SolicitationNotice

buyer: Infrastruttura - Progetti di ampliamento e rinnovo - Gestione del progetto - regione sud
title: AS25 Lugano-Melide, binari di giro corsa Parte 2: FASE 1 + FASE 2 - Opere da impresario costruttore
description:
Le présent contrat a pour objet l’exécution des prestations nécessaires à la réalisation des travaux d’agrandissement, d’adaptation et de modernisation de la gare ferroviaire de Melide, dans le cadre du projet Partie 2 – Phases 1 et 2.

Les travaux comprennent principalement la réalisation et l’adaptation des voies de circulation, de garage et de rebroussement, la construction et l’adaptation des quais ainsi que des infrastructures d’accès conformément à la législation sur l’accessibilité des personnes en situation de handicap, ainsi que l’exécution des ouvrages de génie civil, ferroviaires, techniques et accessoires nécessaires pour garantir l’exploitation du trafic voyageurs longue distance, le garage et la gestion des convois, l’adaptation des infrastructures existantes et le plein respect des dispositions techniques et réglementaires en vigueur.

Sont également comprises les prestations relatives à l’adaptation du passage inférieur existant, du hall d’accès à la gare, des chemins de service ainsi que des autres infrastructures fonctionnellement liées au projet.

title: Berne, Bremgartenstrasse 131-137, gymnase de Neufeld, rénovation et construction de remplacement, CFC 245 Installations mécaniques d’extraction de fumée et de chaleur (IMEFC), SP 2
description: Construction, livraison, paramétrage, contrôle et mise en service du système de commande IMEFC pour les installations mécaniques d’extraction de fumée et de chaleur de l’atrium du bâtiment sud. Les prestations comprennent la centrale IMEFC avec l’ensemble d’appareils de commutation, les modules de commande et de fonction, l’alimentation électrique, les batteries de secours, la protection contre les surtensions, les dispositifs de commande et d’affichage ainsi que l’ensemble des interfaces avec l’installation de détection d’incendie, le système d’automation du bâtiment et les composants de champ fournis par le client. Le système de commande doit être conçu pour le contrôle et la surveillance des ventilateurs de désenfumage, des convertisseurs de fréquence et des ouvertures d’aération motorisées. Les prestations comprennent la planification de l’ouvrage et de l’exécution du fournisseur IMEFC, le paramétrage, la documentation, les contrôles, les tests des points de données et des interfaces, la mise en service, l’attestation de fonctionnement ainsi que la formation du personnel d’exploitation. L’ensemble des composants et des prestations annexes nécessaires au fonctionnement optimal et conforme aux normes doit être pris en compte.

title: Netherlands – Road transport services – Besloten Buspendeldienst TESO veerhaven Texel– Joost Dourleinkazerne V.V.
description: Het doel van de Aanbestedende dienst is het sluiten van een Raamovereenkomst met één Opdrachtnemer voor de verzorging van een Besloten Buspendeldienst. De Raamovereenkomst wordt gesloten voor een periode van 4 jaar waarbij na de eerste twee (2) jaar de mogelijkheid bestaat om de Overeenkomst eenzijdig op te zeggen. De opdracht omvat het vervoeren van medewerkers van het Ministerie van Defensie vanaf TESO veerhaven Texel naar de Joost Dourleinkazerne te Texel en vice versa, van maandag t/m vrijdag, exclusief feestdagen, op vaste tijden. De Aanbestedende dienst wil op werkdagen, exclusief feestdagen, gebruik maken van de dienstverlening. Het gaat om dagelijks 2 ritten van TESO veerhaven Texel naar Joost Dourleinkazerne te Texel en vice versa. Op de eerste woensdag van de maand gaat het om een extra rit. Het Besloten Busvervoer van Defensiemedewerkers geschiedt conform een vaste dienstregeling. De eisen die de Aanbestedende dienst aan de opdracht stelt en de condities waaronder deze moet worden uitgevoerd, zijn uitgewerkt in de bijbehorende aanbestedingsstukken.

title: Pre-solicitation Notice: On-Ramp for the Department of Defense OMNIBUS IV Multiple-Award Contract
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice to synopsize the intention of the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for an on-ramp to the OMNIBUS IV Multiple Award, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle covering military medical research and development services. The eventual RFP will be set-aside for small businesses certified under the Small Business Administration 8(a) Program. The Government anticipates making multiple new awards under this on-ramp, and all new awards will align with the existing unrestricted contract vehicle. This notice is not a request for proposals and does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement. The OMNIBUS IV contract vehicle was awarded under full and open competition with a base ordering period of 20 June 2022 through 19 June 2027 and an Option Ordering Period of 20 June 2027 ? 19 June 2032. Task orders may be competed under fair opportunity (providing all Contract Holders within a Market Segment the opportunity to submit a proposal) or an exception to fair opportunity (such as set-asides for small businesses or applicable small business socioeconomic categories). The cumulative ceiling of this unrestricted IDIQ contract vehicle is $10 billion. To date, the accumulated awarded task order value (including future unexercised option periods) is over $600 million across 51 task orders. Task Orders have been issued by a growing number of end users including DHACA, the U.S. Army Medical Research Acquisition Activity (now integrated into DHACA), the Naval Supply Systems Command, and the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences. When excluding the task orders simply providing a minimum guarantee to the existing Contract Holders, 51 task orders have been issued off this contract vehicle with 8 task orders being set aside for the 8(a) Program and 9 task orders being awarded to an 8(a) Participant. 33 task orders have been awarded so far to small businesses under this contract vehicle. Of the 51 task orders, 94% were awarded during the Government Fiscal Years 2024 - 2026, and the amount of competitive task orders has grown each fiscal year. The Government anticipates releasing the formal RFP for the OMNIBUS IV on-ramp on SAM.gov around late January 2026 (at least 15 calendar days from the posting of this notice. Please see attachments for further details.

title: BEACH RENOURISHMENT OCEAN RIDGE, PALM BEACH COUNTY, FLORIDA
description: The project will renourish approximately 1.1 miles of shoreline in Palm Beach County, within the Town of Ocean Ridge. The Ocean Ridge beach renourishment is located between Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Range Monuments R-153 and R-159. The sand for the project will be sourced from two offshore borrow areas. The north borrow area is located approximately 0.78 nautical miles from the midpoint of the project fill area. The south borrow area is located approximately 0.5 nautical miles from the midpoint of the project fill area. Work also includes but is not limited to environmental species monitoring, hardbottom monitoring, turbidity monitoring, beach tilling, beach fill quality control, screening, and vibration control and monitoring.

title: Defense Innovation Unit Commercial Solutions Opening
description: The Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) is interested in awarding funding agreements (Agreements) to nontraditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DoD), or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the Armed Forces of the United States. As such, DIU hereby announces the release of their streamlined Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). This CSO is seeking proposals for innovative, commercial technologies that accelerate attainment of asymmetric defense capabilities. In this context, innovative means any new technology, process, or business practice, or any new application of an existing technology, process, or business practice that contributes to the sustainment of global peace and U.S. national security. Agreements will be sought under an open (available for five (5) years), competitive (solution brief/demonstration followed by proposal) CSO. This CSO is considered a competitive process, intended to ensure that competitive procedures are used to the maximum extent practicable when entering into Agreements to carry out these prototype projects. Interested parties with current or new/developmental innovative technological solutions or enhancements are highly encouraged to visit the DIU website to obtain more information regarding the process of presenting their solutions to DIU and the potential for securing said Agreements under this CSO. Topic Areas of Interest (AoI) will be posted on the DIU website and may be updated at any time. Please note that the submission period for solution briefs under the identified AOI's will be open for a limited period of time, so check the DIU website for updates frequently. DIU's website is: https://www.diu.mil/work-with-us

title: Netherlands – Repair and maintenance services – Heraanbesteding Vervanging Verlichting Centrum-Parkeergarage Etten-Leur
description: De gemeente Etten-Leur heeft in het centrum van Etten-Leur een ondergrondse parkeergarage met een capaciteit van 1000 parkeerplaatsen. De gemeente is voornemens de bestaande verlichting te vervangen door LED-verlichting, deze deels uit te breiden waar nodig en een bijbehorend meerjarig onderhoudsplan te laten opstellen. Gedurende de uitvoering van de werkzaamheden zal de parkeergarage in gebruik blijven. Het is dus belangrijk dat veiligheid en overlast zoveel mogelijk beperkt blijft. Met de toepassing van LED-armaturen levert de gemeente een bijdrage aan de te bereiken doelstellingen op het gebied van energiebesparing. Ook geeft deze vervanging meer zichtbaarheid in de parkeergarage. De werkzaamheden bestaan in hoofdzaak uit: - Het leveren en vervangen van alle bestaande armaturen door LED-verlichting; - Het uitbreiden van de bestaande verlichtingsinstallatie volgens bijgevoegd verlichtingsplan; - Het installeren van een bedieningsinstallatie/paneel; - Het bedrijfsklaar opleveren van de verlichtingsinstallatie; - Het aanleveren van revisiegegevens; - Het opstellen van een meerjarig onderhoudsplan (15 jaar) t.b.v de LED-verlichting. Voor de uitvoering dient van de bestaande infrastructuur te worden uitgegaan. Uitzondering hierop is de uitbreiding van de bestaande verlichtingsinstallatie volgens verlichtingsplan. De volgende hoeveelheden zijn van toepassing: Conform het Prijzenblad met hoeveelheden (Bijlage a) gaat het om het leveren en installeren van in totaal 1310 stuks armaturen.

title: Switzerland – Data services – (26163) 998 Technikpartner WEB
description: L'Inspection fédérale de la sécurité nucléaire (IFSN) est tenue de fournir des informations au public et aux autorités. Le site web de l'IFSN met à la disposition du public toutes les informations pertinentes et comprend une rubrique « Actualités » ainsi que des contenus statiques tels que des pages, des documents et le Forum technique. Le site web respecte les directives de la Confédération en matière d’identité visuelle (CI) et de conception (CD) et est multilingue (allemand, français, italien et anglais). Des contenus sont également disponibles en « langue simplifiée » et en « langue des signes ». L’IFSN exploite les trois sites web ENSI, ENSI-RAT et EGT-Suisse sur une base technique uniforme avec une configuration WordPress multisite, un design cohérent, des plugins spécifiques à l’IFSN et des interfaces vers des systèmes externes. L’infrastructure d’hébergement, dotée de différents environnements de développement, garantit un fonctionnement sécurisé. L’appel d’offres a pour objectif le changement de partenaire technique et d’hébergement, ainsi que la mise en place d’un « darksite » autonome pouvant être activé en cas d’urgence ou de crise. Nous recherchons un partenaire technique chargé de l’exploitation sécurisée, de la maintenance et du développement de l’infrastructure technique. Cela comprend la gestion des sites web existants, la migration vers un partenaire d’hébergement adapté, ainsi que la gestion de projet et la mise en œuvre du « darksite ».

title: Germany – Tiling work – SKL - Neubau Eltern-Kind-Zentrum am Städtischen Klinikum Lüneburg
description: Das Städtische Klinikum Lüneburg (SKL) ist ein Krankenhaus der Schwerpunktversorgung. Es versorgt einen zunehmend großen Teil der Bevölkerung im nordöstlichen Niedersachsen und beschäftigt über 1.500 Mitarbeiter. Als akademisches Lehrkrankenhaus des Universitäts-klinikums Hamburg-Eppendorf (UKE) ist es mit derzeit 527 Planbetten im Krankenhausbedarfsplan des Landes Niedersachsen ausgewiesen. Das Klinikum verfügt über ein breites medizinisches Leistungsspektrum. Das Städtische Klinikum Lüneburg plant am Standort Lüneburg ein Eltern-Kind-Zentrum als eigenständigen Erweiterungsbaustein der Kinder- und Jugendmedizin sowie der Gynäkologie und Geburtshilfe. Als solches beherbergt es die Entbindungsstation mit sieben Kreißsälen. Das Klinikum verfügt über ein breites medizinisches Leistungsspektrum. Das Städtische Klinikum Lüneburg plant am Standort Lüneburg ein Eltern-Kind-Zentrum als eigenständigen Erweiterungsbaustein der Kinder- und Jugendmedizin sowie der Gynäkologie und Geburtshilfe. buyer: Inspection fédérale de la sécurité nucléaire IFSN
title: (26163) 998 Partenaire technique WEB
description:
L'Inspection fédérale de la sécurité nucléaire (IFSN) est tenue de fournir des informations au public et aux autorités. Le site web de l'IFSN met à la disposition du public toutes les informations pertinentes et comprend une rubrique « Actualités » ainsi que des contenus statiques tels que des pages, des documents et le Forum technique.


Le site web respecte les directives de la Confédération en matière d’identité visuelle (CI) et de conception (CD) et est multilingue (allemand, français, italien et anglais). Des contenus sont également disponibles en « langue simplifiée » et en « langue des signes ».


L’IFSN exploite les trois sites web ENSI, ENSI-RAT et EGT-Suisse sur une base technique uniforme avec une configuration WordPress multisite, un design cohérent, des plugins spécifiques à l’IFSN et des interfaces vers des systèmes externes. L’infrastructure d’hébergement, dotée de différents environnements de développement, garantit un fonctionnement sécurisé.


L’appel d’offres a pour objectif le changement de partenaire technique et d’hébergement, ainsi que la mise en place d’un « darksite » autonome pouvant être activé en cas d’urgence ou de crise.


Nous recherchons un partenaire technique chargé de l’exploitation sécurisée, de la maintenance et du développement de l’infrastructure technique. Cela comprend la gestion des sites web existants, la migration vers un partenaire d’hébergement adapté, ainsi que la gestion de projet et la mise en œuvre du « darksite ».

El dossier deberá contener, según resulte aplicable a cada elemento, fotografías, fichas o descripciones técnicas, dimensiones, características constructivas y funcionales, materiales, acabados y cuantos otros datos resulten necesarios para comprobar que los bienes propuestos cumplen las prescripciones mínimas establecidas en el pliego de prescripciones técnicas particulares. En particular, deberá permitir comprobar la adecuación técnica de los principales elementos integrantes del suministro: casetas de madera; elementos luminosos y ornamentales; caseta de Papá Noel y jaima; photocall; árbol de Navidad; pórtico ornamental de bienvenida; letras corporativas iluminadas; escenario; instalación eléctrica temporal; elementos de señalización y protección contra incendios; y aseos portátiles, incluidos los adaptados. La documentación aportada deberá permitir al órgano de contratación comprobar que los bienes que se adscribirán a la ejecución del contrato cumplen las características mínimas exigidas. La falta de presentación de esta documentación por la persona o entidad propuesta como adjudicataria, o su insuficiencia para acreditar el cumplimiento de las especificaciones técnicas mínimas, determinará las consecuencias previstas en la LCSP para la falta de acreditación de los requisitos exigidos con carácter previo a la adjudicación. La solvencia técnica exigida no se fundamenta en la experiencia previa de la persona o entidad licitadora ni se exige una relación de suministros anteriormente ejecutados. title: EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI): ELDERS AND ELDER HELPERS FOR CORRECTIONAL SERVICE OF CANADA INSTITUTIONS IN THE PRAIRIES REGION
description: EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI): ELDERS AND ELDER HELPERS FOR CORRECTIONAL SERVICE OF CANADA INSTITUTIONS IN THE PRAIRIES REGION PURPOSE OF THE EXPRESSION OF INTEREST The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) is asking Elders and Elder Helpers interested in providing Indigenous cultural support and guidance to offenders to contact the CSC Representative identified below. BACKGROUND: CSC has a legal obligation to provide Indigenous offenders with programs and reintegration support that respect Indigenous culture and values. Elders and Elder Helpers provide services under contract to CSC to assist Indigenous offenders in their traditional healing journey, to develop an understanding of traditional Indigenous culture through teachings, guidance, counselling. CSC is committed to providing a variety of rehabilitation programs and opportunities to Indigenous offenders. Elders and Elder Helpers expose individuals and groups of offenders to traditional Indigenous ways of life, based on their own teachings, counselling and traditional ceremonies and practices to promote ongoing healing and balance, and increase the likelihood of successful reintegration. CSC relies on support from First Nation communities, Metis communities, Inuit communities and Indigenous organizations to provide cultural immersion and practices to Indigenous offenders that CSC cannot offer or manage. The Canadian Federal Correctional environment presents challenges in trying to offer Indigenous support and services within institutions due to the constraints of various security levels, the related level of controlled movement of offenders, and other security requirements. CSC has developed policy and guidelines to better support cultural practices and ceremonies. REQUIREMENTS: CSC respects the cultural and traditions of Indigenous communities and strives to treat Elders and Elder Helpers with the utmost respect. Any Elder or Elder Helper interested in providing services to indigenous offenders must be recognized by their Indigenous community as having the knowledge and understanding of the community’s traditional culture, including their ceremonies, protocols, teachings and healing practices, according to their beliefs and social traditions. Knowledge and wisdom are the essential and defining traits Elders and Elder Helpers achieve by following a traditional way of life consistent with the teachings of their community’s Elders and healers over a significant period. Elders and Elder Helpers must be recognized as such by Indigenous communities, other Elders and their teachers. The tasks Elders within CSC typically perform include counselling, teachings, ceremonies and activities for individuals and groups such as: - Providing guidance and teachings through group sessions (circles) and individual discussions with offenders in the institution. - Conducting spiritual services and various traditional ceremonies based on each Elder’s teachings. - Assisting offenders following a healing path in support of their correctional plan. - Escorting offenders on Escorted Temporary Absences (ETAs) for ceremonial and other spiritual purposes as requested and mutually agreed upon. - Providing advice and information to staff and management, locally, regionally and nationally on issues of Indigenous spirituality, cultural practices, ceremonies, ceremonial objects, traditional practices and protocols, traditional medicine or sacred grounds within the institution. This includes the collection and storage of ceremonial objects and traditional and ceremonial medicines. - Introducing institutional staff to various elements of traditional spirituality as deemed appropriate based on the Elder’s teachings. - Participating in case conferences as requested and providing verbal comments to the offender’s Case Management Team regarding the offender’s participation in a healing path and cultural involvement. Elder Helpers within CSC support and assist Elders to facilitate delivery of services and provide support, such as: - Ensuring offenders and staff follow appropriate protocols when approaching the Elder - Ensuring there are adequate supplies of traditional and ceremonial items, materials and medicines for ceremony purposes as requested by the Elder - Coordinating and providing supervision of offenders during ceremonies and assistance at the Elder’s request. Providing performance of ceremonies in the Elder’s absence. This also includes scheduling of ceremonies and providing notification of participants to Elders and staff as required. - Conducting group discussions and teachings, with the Elder’s agreement, in the identification and proper use of ceremonial objects to offenders and staff. - Assisting the Elder in preparing written and verbal reports to support case management teams and participating in staff meetings. - Providing counselling services as directed when the Elder is unavailable. - Providing cultural awareness sessions to staff to promote a culturally safe environment. CONSTRAINTS: Characteristics of the offender population: Along with recognizing the gender, cultural, religious and linguistic differences of inmates, Elders and Elder Helpers must particularly take into consideration the historical context of the lives of Canada’s Indigenous peoples and be sensitive to the impacts of intergenerational trauma and the physical, mental, emotional, and social harms experienced by Indigenous people. Security: As Elders or Elder Helpers under contract to CSC have access to protected information and provide cultural support and guidance within correctional facilities, they are subject to security requirements. They must take measures to protect shared personal and protected information in accordance with the contract’s security requirements. Insurance: Elder and Elder Helpers must comply with CSC’s insurance requirements including Commercial General Liability Insurance and maintain it through the duration of the contract. SUPPORT TO CONTRACTOR: To support Elders and Elder Helpers in providing services to Indigenous Offenders, CSC provides the following: 1. Appropriately equipped facilities for the provision of confidential spiritual services, including the designation of (private) indoor and outdoor space to conduct traditional ceremonies, spiritual activities, and one on one counselling. 2. Ensuring financial and human resources are provided for the gathering of ceremonial objects outside the institution. 3. Ensuring Indigenous Liaison Officers or Parole Officers are available to assist Elders and Elder Helpers in documenting verbal reports Elders and Elder Helpers provide and ensuring the completion of Elder Reviews as per the outline in Commissioner Directive 702 (i.e. Intake, Progress and Decision). 4. Providing orientation to the institution, including all policies and security requirements Elders and Elder Helpers have to follow when carrying out their tasks. 5. Ensuring Elders Elder Helpers are paired with offenders with the same language requirements (French or English). ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS Elders and Elder Helpers providing services to CSC offenders must meet the following essential requirements. CSC reserves the right to modify any and all of these requirements at any time in accordance with its needs. 1. The Elder or Elder Helper must be recognized by their community as an Elder/Elder Helper/Cultural Advisor within that community. 2. The Elder or Elder Helper must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience obtained in the past 10 years in delivering spiritual and cultural services and teachings to Indigenous people. This experience must include: a) providing counselling and guidance according to the traditions and teachings of their own community; and b) being familiar with and able to conduct a variety of ceremonies with a focus on healing according to their own teachings. 3. The Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Fort Drum, NY is seeking multiple businesses willing to enter into a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for services under North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) 561321: Security Systems Services index Fire alarm sales combined with installation, repair, or monitoring services. The small business size standard for this industry is $22.0 million in average annual revenue. Fire Alarm projects would include but are not limited to the following: providing all necessary resources, management, personnel, materials, transportation, supplies, and equipment, except Government Furnished Property (GFP), necessary in repairing, replacing, and reprogramming of fire alarm systems, sprinkler system, security systems, facility access control systems and all associated equipment in facilities on Fort Drum, NY. Insurance is required for these types of projects; a current certification of insurance must be provided prior to receiving a BPA. Some BPA calls may be posted to UNISON, while not required it is encouraged for vendors receiving a BPA to register at UNISON. Registration is free and can be completed at https://www.unisonglobal.com/product-suites/acquisition/marketplace/ Generally some calls placed will be below $25,000, and may be sporadic in nature. The Contractor must be able to accept the Government Purchase Card (GPC) and submit invoices in Wide Area Workflow (WAWF). To register and access WAWF, go to https://wawf.eb.mil/. BPAs will be evaluated annually and may remain in place for up to five years. IAW FAR 52.204-7 interested parties must be registered with the System for Award Management Registration (SAM) under NACIS code 561621. The registrations can be done through System for Award Management (SAM) for free at https://www.sam.gov The Contractor will not receive a BPA until these registrations are completed. Any interested party should submit their DUNS number, CAGE Code, and Tax ID number to SFC Timmons at david.b.timmons.mil@army.mil. Any correspondence relating to this synopsis should have FIRE ALARM BPA notated in the subject field.

title: VI DPC A34(1) � Veterans Drive Contract 2 Improvements to RTE 30
description: Proposals from all Business Concerns will be accepted for Project VI DPC A34(1) � Veterans Drive Contract 2 Improvements to RTE 30. Solicitation Number 693C73-27-R-000012, located in St. Thomas, USVI. The project consists of the reconstruction and addition of new lanes for a continuous four-lane roadway with two lanes in each direction for an approximate distance of 2052 ft. (0.39 mi). The work includes widening and reconstruction of Veterans Drive, enhance pedestrian and vehicular safety, and improve drainage of the roadway and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost for all the work schedules is estimated to be between $80,000,000 to $90,000,000. Contract Award/Notice to Proceed is subject to the receipt of permits. Proposal documents should be issued on or about November 19, 2026. Proposal due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Offerors will be required to submit a technical proposal in addition to cost proposal. The Solicitation will include further information on these requirements. Use Internet address www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will no longer be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. IMPORTANT SUBCONTRACTING PLAN REQUIREMENTS For purposes of this Contract, the DBE subcontracting goal is 32.10 percent (%) as determined by the Virgin Islands Department of Public Works (VIDPW) with the concurrence of the Contracting Officer. This Contract will be awarded only to the responsive and responsible Offeror who meets this goal or who demonstrates good faith efforts to do so. Failure to make a good faith effort is defined as willful or intentional failure to perform in accordance with the requirements of this Contract, or willful or intentional action to frustrate the achievement of the Subcontracting Plan, if applicable. Guidance on what constitutes good faith efforts is described in the VIDPW's approved DBE Program. Copies of the program can be obtained from the VIDPW's DBE Liaison Officer. For copies of the current DBE Directory contact the VIDPW's DBE Liaison Officer. The Contracting Officer, the Contracting Officer�s Representative, and the VIDPW's DBE Liaison Officer are responsible for approving a reasonable and realistic plan. title: Navy Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS) Hardware and Software Production
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Mission Systems is issuing a Full and Open Competitive Solicitation (N00024-26-R-5246) for the development, production, integration, testing, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment of the U.S. Navy Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS) Hardware and Software. This procurement supports PAE Mission Systems structure, the acronym �PMW/A� means Program Manager, Warfighting / Applications (PMW/A 520) Navigation Program requirements for both surface and subsurface platforms. The resultant contract will provide continued production and sustainment of Navy ECDIS Hardware and Software. Hardware Scope: Includes production, sustainment, integration, assembly, and testing. Software Scope: Includes maintenance, modification, upgrades, integration, testing, and delivery of ECDIS software products. These software scope activities will be provided as level-of-effort tasks under Government oversight, with technical support from the Navy ECDIS Systems Engineering and Integration Agent, NSWC Philadelphia, PA. Award is anticipated in Q4 FY27 and will be made to the Offeror whose proposal represents the Best Value to the Government in accordance with FAR 15.101?1. The planned contract structure includes one base year with four one?year option periods, beginning in FY27. Deliveries are anticipated to be FOB Destination.

title: Objektplanung - BBS I, Umsetzung Brandschutzkonzept
description: Die Stadt Delmenhorst hat aufgrund von festgestellten Mängeln bei einer Brandschutzbegehung ein Brandschutzkonzept in Auftrag gegeben. Dieses soll nun bauordnungsrechtlich genehmigt werden und die darin beschriebenen Brandschutzmaßnahmen geplant und umgesetzt werden. Für die Planung der technischen Anlagen in den Gebäuden (Brandwarnanlage, Hausalarmierungsanlage, Sicherheitsstromversorgung, Sicherheitsbeleuchtungsanlagen und elektrische Leitungsanlagen) wird ein Fachplaner hinzugezogen. Für die erforderlichen Maßnahmen wurde im Rahmen des Brandschutzkonzeptes eine Priorisierungsliste erstellt. Die Hauptmaßnahmen hieraus sind die Errichtung von zwei notwendigen Außentreppen als bauliche 2. Flucht- und Rettungswege, die Ertüchtigung der Hausalarmierungsanlage des Hauptgebäudes auf eine Brandwarnanlage mit Sicherheitsstromversorgung, der Einbau einer Hausalarmierungsanlage im Nebengebäude, Einbau von Sicherheitsbeleuchtungsanlagen mit Sicherheitsstromversorgung, Ausführung elektrischer Leitungsanlagen mit Funktionserhalt, Herstellung einer Rauchableitung mit Auslösestellen in einem Treppenraum, Herstellen einer Rauchableitung für den Aufzugschacht im Dach und weitere diverse Brandschutzmaßnahmen, wie z.B. der Austausch von Türen und Verglasungen mit brandschutztechnischer Anforderung oder ein Verschließen ehemaliger Türöffnungen. In bestimmten Bereichen sind Bauteile auf ihre Brandschutzqualität zu überprüfen und ggf. zu ertüchtigen oder in geforderter Qualität zu errichten, dies betrifft insbesondere Leitungsdurchführungen und deren Schottung, Installationsschächte, Entlüftungseinrichtungen innenliegender Bäder und Anschlusspunkte im Bereich der Dächer.

title: PSIB W3048-20KF46 Multipurpose Alpine Military Mobility Training Facility
description: AMENDMENT TO CLOSING TIME: Please disregard the Ariba Discovery posting response deadline closing time and Buyandsell posting closing time. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted on 2027-01-14 by 2:00 P.M. EST. All bids submitted after 2:00 P.M. EST will result in the bid being declared non-responsive. The Department of National Defence (DND) has a requirement for a Contractor to provide the facilities, instructors and equipment to conduct training exercises for up to 14 soldiers in Canada. The training will be focused on the use of various transportation types ranging from person-borne equipment such as skis, to motorized equipment such as snowmobiles and motorcycles, in mountainous and austere terrain during all weather conditions. Some of the exercises will include firing weapons while on the Contractor’s facilities. This Request for Supply Arrangement (RFSA) has two streams. One stream for Indigenous Business Offerors and another for non Indigenous Business Offerors.

Mit Zustimmung seiner Aufsichtsbehörde kann das LZN weitere Aufgaben für öffentlich-rechtliche Bedarfsträger innerhalb und außerhalb der niedersächsischen Landesverwaltung sowie für privatrechtliche Gesellschaften in vollständiger Eigentümerschaft der öffentlichen Hand übernehmen (vgl. § 3 Betriebsanweisung). In dieser Zuständigkeit umfasst der Auftrag den Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung mit einem Unternehmen (§ 21 VgV) über die Lieferung von Wollunterwäsche für die Kooperationspartner der norddeutschen Küstenländer der Polizei und Justiz, der Landesforsten und Ordnungsämtern innerhalb von Deutschland und sonstige Behörden (gemäß Anlage) mit einer Preisbindung von 24 Monaten sowie optional zwei einseitige Vertragsverlängerungen zu jeweils höchstens 12 Monaten mit einem Unternehmen. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind der Leistungsbeschreibung -Technischer Teil (Teil B) inkl. Angebotsvordruck zu entnehmen. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind den technischen Lieferbedingungen und dem Angebotsvordruck zu entnehmen.

description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE CANADIAN PATROL SUBMARINE PROJECT Halifax, NS (with Security Requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Halifax, NS. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested [contractors and consultants] to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: HX26CPSP; Title: Canadian Patrol Submarine Project - Infrastructure Approximate Estimate:  $5B-$10B Anticipated Posting: January 2027 Description: Following the Prime Minister’s announcement on 6 July 2026, Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS) was selected as the preferred supplier to begin negotiations for delivering Canada’s next fleet of submarines. DND needs to be ready with the appropriate enabling infrastructure synchronized with submarine delivery, with boats arriving 2035 or earlier. To support the delivery of the new submarines, DND must deliver complex, multi-site infrastructure at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Halifax at Wright’s Cove by 2033 to enable submarine berthing and maintenance beginning in 2034. The Construction Management (CM) contract will see the construction of jetties, maintenance facilities, training facilities, offices, and a variety of other supporting facilities to support submarine operations and sustainment. This effort will be realized via the execution of a series of successive work packages in Halifax, NS. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS This opportunity is restricted to Canadian, German, and Norwegian firms that meet the security clearance requirements. To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is FACILITY SECURITY CLEARANCE (FSC) at up to level II (SECRET)  4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors  to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. title: Totalberedskap på tvers av landegrenser
description: Totalberedskap på tvers av landegrenser - Kommuner og fylkeskommuner i grenseoverskridende samhandling for styrket beredskap og motstandskraft. KS ønsker å utrede hvilket potensial som ligger i å utvikle totalberedskap gjennom samarbeid på tvers av landegrensene, og ønsker tilbud på et FoU-prosjekt som skal svare ut følgende problemstillinger: - Hvordan kan kommuner/fylkeskommuner på norsk og svensk side utvikle et felles rammeverk for beredskap og krisehåndtering som sikrer effektiv samhandling ved grenseoverskridende hendelser? - Hvilke potensielle gevinster vil et slikt utvidet samarbeid over grensen på beredskapsområdet gi for kommuner, fylkeskommuner, innbyggerne og andre beredskapsak. Prosjektet skal ha både strategisk og operativt perspektiv på beredskapsarbeidet underveis. Herunder spesielt se på hvordan kommunenes operative redningsressurs brann og redning kan bidra til å styrke kommunenes samlede beredskapsevne på tvers av landegrensene, spesielt i situasjoner høyt i krisespekteret.

title: D--USGS L10 MOC & Operations Updates
description: Following the May 2026 RFI feedback and one-on-one meetings with industry, the USGS has matured its acquisition strategy for the Landsat 10 Mission Operations Center and Flight Operations scope of work. USGS intends to procure a new commercial, cloud-based or containerized cloud-native MOC to be hosted using USGS's Cloud Hosting Services (CHS) III services or EROS mission infrastructure Container (Kubernetes) Hosting Solution, respectively. Based on industry feedback and technical study results, the Government is no longer considering the option to augment the existing Landsat 8 and 9 LMOC. Included in this announcement are the following reference materials: 1) Draft MOC/Ops Synopsis Document 2) Draft MOC Requirements Document The Government is not requesting feedback at this time; industry will have an opportunity to provide feedback when the Draft RFP is released. These draft documents build on feedback received in response to the May 2026 RFI and provide industry with additional technical detail to clarify the Government's current approach to the Landsat 10 MOC Development and Operations scope of work. These documents will continue to be refined following the spacecraft award and feedback on the draft RFP leading up to the final RFP release. The MOC functions document previously shared with the RFI has been incorporated into the MOC Synopsis and will no longer be issued as a standalone RFP document. USGS is working toward the following timeline for the RFP surrounding this scope of work: * Draft RFP Release: Estimating early February 2027 (anticipate this will be following spacecraft RFP award) * Industry briefing (virtual): Shortly after Draft RFP announcement * Feedback response period: Anticipated to be 30 days * Tentative one-on-one meetings with contractors as needed to clarify any feedback provided (could be virtual or in-person, at the government's discretion) * Final RFP Release: As soon as possible following updates to documentation based on industry feedback. Estimating May 2027

description: Le présent appel d'offres porte sur des prestations d'entrepreneur général en Suisse alémanique, romande et italienne sous forme d'un contrat-cadre. La durée du contrat est de trois ans, avec une option de prolongation de deux ans supplémentaires. En règle générale, l’attribution du mandat intervient à partir de la phase partielle SIA 51 (projet d’exécution). Dans certains cas, l’implication préalable de l’entreprise est nécessaire afin d’établir la planification des phases de construction pendant les phases partielles 31-33. Il n’existe aucune obligation d’achat pour CFF SA (aucune prétention quant à l’atteinte du montant du contrat d’ici à la fin de la durée contractuelle, option comprise). Contenu de ce lot : Type/genre : Marché spécifique pour le remplacement du ballast (SE) et la rénovation de la plateforme (UBS) des voies et des appareils de voie, à l'échelle de la Suisse. Description : Lot SE/UBS spécialisé pour des projets ferroviaires (comprenant en partie des appareils de voie) d'une longueur comprise entre environ 1 000 m et 9 000 m maximum. Des travaux de génie civil sont également à réaliser. Particularités : Aucun criblage n’est à réaliser. Volume/quantité : Volume annuel d'environ 5 à 10 km de remplacement de ballast et de l'assainissement de la plateforme ferroviaire. Quantité minimale d'achat annuelle garantie de 5 km/an de l'assainissement de la plateforme ferroviaire. Il n'y a pas de quantité minimale d'achat pour un simple remplacement de ballast (sans assainissement de la plateforme ferroviaire). Le volume annuel théorique maximal correspond au double de la quantité minimale d'achat, soit 10 km/an de réfection de la couche de fondation. Cette valeur est déterminante pour le rabais de quantité. Adjudication : Une seule adjudication.

title: Switzerland – Building construction work – Pächterried Provisorium 2027 (Modulbau, Container), Regensdorf
description: Die Gemeinde Regensdorf verzeichnet seit mehreren Jahren ein anhaltendes Bevölkerungs- wachstum. Für den Standort Pächterried wird des- halb zusätzlicher Schulraum sowie Raum für die schulergänzende Betreuung (SeB) benötigt. Zur kurzfristigen Deckung des ausgewiesenen Raumbedarfs beabsichtigt die Gemeinde Regens- dorf, angrenzend an dem Areal der Schulanlage Pächterried ein entsprechendes Provisorium (voraussichtlich für die Dauer von 5 Jahren) zu erstellen. Gesucht wird eine einfache, funktionale und wirtschaftliche Modul- oder auch Containerlösung, die sich rasch realisieren lässt und einen sicheren, kindergerechten Betrieb ermöglicht. Die Wiederverwendung einer bestehenden An- lage ist zulässig, sofern sämtliche Anforderungen dieses Pflichtenhefts erfüllt werden.
